correctness.rationale: For a binary word of known n with m=|w|a≥1, m≤|w|b, the run decomposition b^s0 a b^s1 ... a b^sm is bijective with nonnegative integer vectors sum s_j=n-m. The scattered coefficient y_l=binom(w,a^l b)=sum_{j≥l} C(j,l)s_j for l=0..m-1 (l=0 supplied by known n,m). The first m columns of the m×(m+1) truncated Pascal matrix are unimodular triangular, so rank m and integral kernel generated by v_j=(-1)^j C(m,j), which has coordinate ±1. Thus all integer solutions are s+t v, t∈Z; positivity imposes -Te≤t≤To, Te min even floor(s_j/C(m,j)), To min odd similarly, producing exact class size 1+Te+To and iff uniqueness Te=To=0. Independently checked Pascal nullspaces/ranks for m1..10 and complete 1024 direct-word collision fibers for length n<=10 with independent scattered-subsequence recurrence. No dependence on finite enumeration for the all-n claim.
